messages:
Ethan: Hey team, just booted my assigned MacBook (M1) and the MDM says enrolled but I can't install the company VPN certs  Keychain keeps asking for my login password repeatedly and then fails. Also FileVault asked for a recovery key during setup but the onboarding doc only mentions "we escrow keys"  where do I find it?

IT Support: Welcome, Ethan. Can you share the output of:

```
profiles status -type enrollment
fdesetup status
security find-certificate -a -c redwood-device-ca
```

and confirm whether you're logging in with the desktop account or your SSO account? Sometimes macOS creates a local account that isn't linked to the SSO user.

Ethan: Pasting outputs: profiles shows "Enrolled (MDM)" and one profile pending user approval. fdesetup status: FileVault is On. The certificate command returns the cert but marked as untrusted. I'm signing in with my SSO (okta) email and password.

Rosa: Hi @Ethan 020202this "pending user approval" is the culprit. You need to manually approve the device profile so the cert can be trusted by the system keychain. I can push a one-hour temporary admin elevation to your device if you want to approve now.

Ethan: That would be great, thanks.

Device Ops: Temporary admin granted to Ethan for 45 minutes. Steps for approval:
1) System Settings 1010Profiles -> select "Redwood Device Management" -> Install.
2) When Keychain prompt appears, enter your login password and choose "Always Allow" for the company CA cert.
3) Restart and re-run `security find-certificate -a -c redwood-device-ca` to confirm trust status shows "trusted".

Ethan: Installing now. Quick question 020202 the Keychain prompt asks for a credential to allow access for "VPN Client" 020202 is it safe to approve?

Security Eng: Yes, safe. Confirm the cert issuer is "redwood-device-ca" and that SANs include "vpn.redwood.ai". If anything differs, don't approve and ping us.

Ethan: Cert shows issuer redwood-device-ca and SAN includes vpn.redwood.ai. Approved and selected Always Allow. Installer finished. Rebooting.

Device Ops: After reboot, run `profiles status -type configuration` and `fdesetup status` then paste output so we can mark the device compliant and revoke admin.

Ethan: profiles: all profiles installed, no pending user approval. fdesetup status: FileVault is On for the disk. security find-certificate now shows redwood-device-ca as trusted.

Device Ops: Thanks 020202 revoking temporary admin and marking device compliant in console.

Ethan: One last thing 020202 where can I view the escrowed FileVault recovery key? Not necessary now but want to know for future.

IT Support: We don't surface the recovery key to users. It's escrowed to our MDM/KMS and can be retrieved by IT/Security for device recovery following approval. If you need it for a password reset scenario we'll coordinate via support ticket.

Ethan: Got it, thanks everyone for the quick help and welcome messages!

IT Support: Welcome aboard, Ethan! If you hit any more setup hiccups this week ping here or DM @it-support. :party_popper:
